De capienda ex inimicis utilitate
Abhandlung des Plutarch: darüber, dass jemand von seinem Feinde Nutzen hat
A Tract of Plutarch on the Advantage to Be Derived by a Man from His Enemy
bibl.author: Plutarch

noteGrp.note: An anonymous Syriac translation of Plutarch's moral treatise De capienda ex inimicis utilitate, freely adapted for a Christian readership. The translator removes references to pagan religion and Greek mythology, and replaces many proper names with generic figures such as a king, a wise man or a judge. On grounds of language and translation technique, the translation was probably made in the fifth or early sixth century. It survives in a single manuscript, Sinai syr. 16, a monastic anthology of the late sixth or seventh century that also contains two other Syriac texts under Plutarch's name, De cohibenda ira and De exercitatione.
